headline.purpose: Section titles and the About heading.

body.purpose: About copy, job and project descriptions.

label.purpose: Small chrome text, 0.82–0.95rem by context: job dates and nav links at 0.95rem; chips, footer links, project links, toast, and slider count at 0.82–0.9rem.

shadows.name: ambient-lift
shadows.purpose: Spotlight shadow for featured surfaces: hero image, photo frame, active project slide.

shadows.name: control-shadow
shadows.purpose: Resting shadow for small circular nav controls.

motion.name: ease-reveal
motion.purpose: Scroll-reveal fade + rise for sections and cards.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Main call-to-action button — pill-shaped, cobalt fill.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-block; padding: 14px 28px; border-radius: 999px; font-weight: 600; font-size: 0.95rem; background: var(--color-primary); color: #fff; border: 2px solid transparent; transition: transform 0.2s ease, background 0.2s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover, .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { background: var(--color-primary-dark); transform: translateY(-2px); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #fff; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Secondary action button — transparent fill, midnight border, fills solid on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { display: inline-block; padding: 14px 28px; border-radius: 999px; font-weight: 600; font-size: 0.95rem; color: var(--color-dark); border: 2px solid var(--color-dark); background: transparent; transition: background 0.2s ease, color 0.2s ease; } .ds-btn-outline:hover, .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { background: var(--color-dark); color: #fff; }

components.name: Resume Link (Dark)
components.description: Signature exception to the pill shape — square-cornered, stamped-credential feel for the resume link.
components.css: .ds-btn-dark { display: inline-block; padding: 8px 28px; border-radius: 0; font-weight: 600; font-size: 0.95rem; background: var(--color-dark); color: #fff; transition: background 0.2s ease; } .ds-btn-dark:hover, .ds-btn-dark:focus-visible { background: #000; }

components.name: Chip
components.description: Small tech-tag pill used under job entries and project details.
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-block; background: #fff; border: 1px solid var(--color-border); border-radius: 999px; padding: 6px 14px; font-size: 0.82rem; font-weight: 600; color: var(--color-dark); }

components.description: Transient confirmation message, pill-shaped, midnight fill, floating shadow.

narrative.overview:
This isn't a portfolio that describes skill — it's one that demonstrates it. Every scroll reveal, every timed transition, every pixel of a card's border-radius is itself the evidence a recruiter is evaluating, alongside the words on the page. The system reads as corporate-editorial confidence: a strong cobalt anchors action, midnight ink carries weight and authority, and everything else steps back into quiet neutrals so the craft — not the color — does the convincing.

The system explicitly rejects the generic, unmodified template look. Nothing here should feel like a free Bootstrap portfolio with the name swapped in. It also rejects gimmick for its own sake: motion and decoration earn their place only when they reinforce precision and credibility, never novelty for its own sake, per the anti-reference already set in PRODUCT.md.
keyCharacteristics: Confident, precise, minimal — restraint reads as competence to this audience.
One accent color (cobalt) carries almost all interactive weight; midnight carries authority and structure.
Soft, ambient, navy-tinted shadows lift key surfaces (hero image, photo frame, active project slide) off a flat, mostly-white canvas.
Motion is a reveal, not a performance: content fades and rises into place once, on scroll, then gets out of the way.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Cobalt is the only color that means "click me." If a new interactive element needs a color, it's cobalt or it's midnight-on-hover — never a third hue.

rules.name: The Warmth-in-Moderation Rule
rules.body: The amber and lavender gradient blobs behind the About photo are the system's only departure from blue/neutral. They exist to add a trace of humanity against an otherwise corporate palette — but they are a whisper, not a shout: low opacity (~0.5), softened saturation, confined to that one moment on the page.

rules.name: The Weight-Over-Size Rule
rules.body: Emphasis comes from jumping to 700–800 weight, not from introducing a new font size outside the hierarchy.

rules.name: The Spotlight, Not Drop-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Ambient Lift is reserved for content the visitor should look at, never for structural containers like nav or footer. If everything is elevated, nothing is.

rules.name: The Sanctioned Exception Rule
rules.body: Two sizes sit outside the type ramp entirely, by design, each used exactly once: the header wordmark (800, 1.25rem) and the slider's nav-arrow glyph (1.1rem). Neither is a role to reuse elsewhere.

dos: Do keep cobalt as the only color that signals "actionable" — buttons, active links, hover states.
Do use the pill shape (999px) for standard buttons and chips; reserve square corners for the one deliberate exception (the resume link).
Do reserve Ambient Lift shadows for featured content only (hero image, photo frame, active project slide) — never for structural chrome.
Do let real, verifiable proof (live project links, GitHub) carry the Projects and Experience sections, per PRODUCT.md's "verifiable over descriptive" principle.
Do keep the header's Contact link reachable at every scroll position — PRODUCT.md's belief ladder depends on it.
donts: Don't let this read as a generic, unmodified template portfolio — no stock Bootstrap card grids, no default framework styling left unclaimed.
Don't add gimmicky or novelty visual effects — bouncing icons, confetti, cartoonish illustration — anything that trades credibility for cuteness with a recruiter audience.
Don't introduce a third accent hue outside cobalt/midnight for interactive elements.
Don't let the About section's decorative amber/lavender blobs grow louder than a whisper — keep opacity low and saturation soft; they're a signature detail, not a focal point.
Don't apply Ambient Lift-style shadows to everything — if every card floats, the featured surfaces stop feeling featured.
